#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: -N 1
#flux: --ntasks-per-node=1
#flux: --cpus-per-task=1
#flux: -t 04:00:00

# The original script specified multiple partitions; the last one ('batch') is chosen.
# The 'devel' partition was commented out.
#flux: -q batch

# The Slurm reservation directive is translated.
#flux: --reservation=debug

# CRITICAL: The following resource requests from Slurm could not be translated and have been OMITTED.
# These are highly site-specific. This job will likely FAIL without them.
# The job will NOT be allocated a GPU (specifically a 'pascal' type) and will NOT be allocated 15GB of memory.
# #SBATCH --gres=gpu:pascal:1
# #SBATCH --mem=15GB

source load_modules_qbig_pascal.sh
#export KOKKOS_PROFILE_LIBRARY=/hiskp4/garofalo/chemHMC/code/external/kokkos-tools/kp_memory_events.so
# export KOKKOS_PROFILE_LIBRARY=/hiskp4/garofalo/chemHMC/code/external/kokkos-tools/kp_kernel_logger.so

 
#rm rng* out_xyz.txt
# The original script body was entirely commented out. The lines are preserved as comments.
#/qbigwork/garofalo/valgrind/install_dir/bin/valgrind --leak-check=full ../../chemHMC/code/build/main//main -i input_I.yaml
#../../chemHMC/code/build/main//main -i input_I.yaml
#main/main -i ../test.yaml
#./test/test 
#./test/test_binning -i ../test.yaml

reasons: Validation failed at directives: --ntasks-per-node=1, --cpus-per-task=1. The standard short-form options ('-n', '-c') are more portable and widely supported.
Validation failed at directive: --reservation=debug. Reservation IDs are site-specific and cannot be validated in a generic context.
issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, two essential resource requests from the original Slurm script were omitted: the request for a Pascal GPU (`--gres=gpu:pascal:1`) and the request for 15GB of memory (`--mem=15GB`). While the translated script is syntactically valid (aside from the reasons noted above), it is functionally incorrect. It will not be allocated a GPU and will receive a default, likely insufficient, memory allocation. Both omissions will almost certainly cause the job to fail at runtime.
The entire execution body of the script is commented out. As written, the job will allocate resources and then do nothing.
